title: Build a CMOS inverter
concept: A single input selects either the PMOS pull-up or NMOS pull-down. A standard-cell interface exposes signal pins separately from VPWR and VGND.
question: Which transistor charges Y when A is low?
explanation: A low gate voltage turns on the PMOS and turns off the NMOS.
repair: Select MP_A in the schematic. In Properties, change its gate terminal net to A and apply the edit. Confirm both drains meet at Y and the body pins go to their supply rails.
reflection: Describe the pull-up and pull-down paths, then explain why a library cell needs named power pins and accessible signal pins.

title: Build a two-input NAND
concept: A NAND uses two series NMOS devices to pull down and two parallel PMOS devices to pull up. A series stack adds resistance when it conducts.
question: At which input combination does the NAND discharge Y?
explanation: Both gates must be high to turn on the full series NMOS path.
repair: Select MN_B and change its gate terminal net to B. Trace the NMOS stack from Y through N_STACK to VGND. Confirm the two PMOS sources both connect to VPWR.
reflection: Use the waveform to explain which vector turns on the NMOS stack. Describe how extra stack resistance could affect a falling output edge.

title: Build a two-input NOR
concept: NOR swaps the series and parallel networks of NAND. Its series PMOS path must charge the output through both devices at the all-zero vector.
question: Which network contains the series stack in a two-input NOR?
explanation: Both PMOS devices conduct together only when A and B are low.
repair: Select MN_B and change its gate terminal net to B. Follow the pull-up from VPWR through P_STACK to Y. Confirm either NMOS can connect Y directly to VGND.
reflection: Compare the PMOS series stack in NOR with the NMOS series stack in NAND. Which edge charges the output capacitor through two devices?

title: Build an AND-OR-invert cell
concept: AOI21 implements Y = NOT((A AND B) OR C) in one complementary network. An NMOS on C bypasses the A/B series path.
question: What is Y when C is high, for any values of A and B?
explanation: C alone enables a pull-down path, and its complementary PMOS blocks the pull-up.
repair: Select MN_C and change its gate terminal net to C. Trace its direct path from Y to VGND, then trace the other path through MN_A and MN_B.
reflection: Name the vectors where C overrides the A/B network. Explain why the A and B inputs can have different timing from C.

title: Build a transmission-gate multiplexer
concept: Complementary transmission gates pass both logic levels. The selected data path drives an internal node, and a two-inverter buffer restores the output.
question: What should the output follow when S is high?
explanation: The S-controlled transmission gate selects B, while the A gate is disabled.
repair: Select MN_B and change its gate terminal net to S. Select MP_B and set its gate terminal net to S_B. Trace A and B to SELECTED and then through the two restoring inverters to Y.
reflection: Compare vectors with different A and B levels. Explain why the PMOS and NMOS use opposite control signals and why the output is buffered.

title: Build a rising-edge D flip-flop
concept: Two level-sensitive transmission-gate latches form a rising-edge storage cell. The master tracks D when CLK is low and the slave updates from the master when CLK rises.
question: What happens if D falls while CLK stays high after a rising edge?
explanation: The master latch has closed, so the slave still sees the value captured at the edge.
repair: Select MN_S_IN and MP_S_IN. Change the s terminal net of both devices from M1 to M2. M1 is the inverted master node, while M2 carries the stored data that should enter the slave.
reflection: Compare Q before and after the second rising clock edge, then explain why Q holds when D changes between edges.
